tally: Ten people, still bootstrapped, and the founders say 43% of new users now arrive through AI search.
supademo: Sales and onboarding teams send an interactive walkthrough instead of a static deck. Free side tools sit in front and feed the paid product.
plutio: A freelancer otherwise keeps proposals in one app, contracts in another, and invoices in a third. Plutio is that whole pile in one login, at a size a solo founder can still imagine copying.
anonymous-workforce-management-saas: The largest Stripe-verified figure in this set has no public name and no website. Employers have been paying it for scheduling and compliance since 2021, and the listing stays anonymous.
myplots: The money is a cut of the ticket, 20% plus a dollar, not a monthly plan. That is why the last 30 days show hundreds of thousands of dollars while recurring revenue reads as zero.
supliful: A creator can put their name on a product while someone else makes and ships it. The work is operations, which is why a plan that starts near $69 a month has piled up tens of millions all-time.
salesrobot: It runs LinkedIn outreach and cold email, and customers pay for credits rather than a seat. The Stripe record shows usage, not a neat subscriber count.
codedex: Beginners practice inside a game, then a club pass starts around $9.99 a month. Thousands of those small memberships are what the revenue figure is adding up.
flocksy: The price is a studio retainer, from about $1,199 a month, because what you buy is a queue of designers and editors. A founder AMA put the team past 70 people.
mycater: Office managers already order catering every week. MyCater takes a cut of that spend, which is why the last 30 days show about $76k while recurring revenue reads as zero.
stan: Creators already need somewhere to get paid. Stan is that checkout, and the last Stripe snapshot put it near $3.57M in monthly revenue. The key expired in April 2026, so the figure is a snapshot.
windmill-growth: Founders pay about $3,999 a month so someone else writes their LinkedIn posts. Seventy-nine of those retainers are what the Stripe record is adding up.
prosp: Sales teams pay for LinkedIn outreach, and the listing itself is for sale. The Stripe key expired in February 2026, so the monthly figure is the last verified snapshot.
dataexpert-techcreator: Students pay about $119 a month for data and AI courses. Hundreds of those memberships are what the revenue figure is adding up.
controlresell: Resellers pay between $30 and $120 a month so the tool posts, negotiates, and relists for them. The Stripe record shows 442 of those subscriptions.
myfrank: Each employee gets a QR code and a challenge for collecting Google reviews. The founder has put the product up for sale.
image-charts: Developers still need a chart that shows up inside an email. The monthly figure is about $6.3k, and the all-time total has been compounding since 2017.
geswork: French service companies pay for scheduling, documents, and billing in one login. The same founder also runs Valideo, a field-report product with its own Stripe record.
mon-atelier: Repair shops in France pay from €19 a month for tickets, invoices, and the compliance ledger. One person runs it, and the founder says 48 shops signed up with no marketing spend.
